dc2F_adrift:
Adrift at sea — multi-day starvation sequence after the ship is set adrift.

The longest cutscene script in the game (~608 lines). Covers the
crew's days of drifting: day-by-day text transitions, starvation
mechanics that damage the player's HP, enemy stat changes for
the weakening crew, palette fades to represent passing time,
and the eventual rescue. Uses hpToHeal for visual HP
drain effects. Includes
player_transition_handlers for cutscene movement control.
dc2F_adrift_fx:
Ocean wave visual effects during the adrift sequence.

Loads spriteset_adrift_wave misc data and plays a looping wave
animation overlay using ResetSpriteInit and LoadSpriteAnimGlobal.
Provides the atmospheric ocean surface effect during the drift.
dc30_dog:
Turbo the dog in Oakton — Kara's dog companion.

Simple NPC. Says: "Woof woof!!" Kara introduces him:
"This dog's name is Turbo. Isn't he cute?" Part of the
Oakton landing scene after the Gold Ship drift.
dc30_kara:
Kara in Oakton — introduces Turbo and suggests exploring.

NPC at the Oakton exterior. Says: "This dog's name is Turbo.
Isn't he cute? Well, let's go. Maybe we can find out where
we are." Transitions from the adrift rescue to Freejia.
dc31_kara:
Kara in the Oakton interior — wakes Will after the shipwreck rescue.

Long cutscene NPC (~85 lines). Kara shouts: "Will! Will!! Wake up!
We've reached land!! We're saved!" Will responds groggily.
Kara explains they're at the home of a man who rescued them.
Multi-phase scene with joypad lock and music changes.
dc31_rescuer:
Rescuer in the Oakton interior — the man who saved Will and Kara.

NPC who wakes Will: "You can wake him up now. He'll be fine
if he takes vitamins." Then: "This is the south outskirts of
Oakton. The city of Freejia is to the north." Establishes
the geographic context and sends the party toward Freejia.
dm_mine_static_prop: Static decorative prop in the Diamond Mine inner area. Non-interactive scene element.
dm3E_intro:
Will's inner monologue on first entering the Diamond Mine and the Sky Garden.

Locks the joypad ($CFFC) and branches on sceneCurrent. Scene $3E (mine entrance) plays the "Diamond Mine was as quiet as a tomb" narration under flag $6A; scene $4C (Sky Garden) plays the "strange garden floating in the sky over Nazca" narration under flag $6B. With the flag clear the actor sets it, waits #1D ticks and prints the dialog; with it set, or in any other scene, the actor unlocks the joypad and dies. Both flags are persistent and never cleared, so each narration plays once per game. The Freejia slave market actors also read $6A.
dm3F_elevator_door:
Elevator entrance door in the mine main area — requires Elevator Key.

Interactable door sprite. If player has the Elevator Key (#0F)
equipped, consumes it, sets flag $69, and shows "You used the
elevator key!" text. Otherwise shows "There's one keyhole in this
door." Once flag $69 is set, applies BG change #7B to open the
passage and sets flag word $017B.
dm3F_elevator_sign:
Elevator entrance sign — readable wall sign in the mine main area.

Solid interactable sprite. When examined, displays:
"(Elevator Entrance) Use that door to get to the elevator."
dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger:
Cave-in trigger in the mine main chamber — collapses the tunnel entrance on the 4th switch hit.

Dies at once when flag word $0121 is set. Otherwise it checks each frame whether the hit counter byte $0A01 (written by dm3F_switch) equals 4. On the frame it does, it sets $0121, applies BG change #21 to redraw the collapsed tunnel entrance and plays rumble sound #0E on both channels; the actor then marks itself for death.
dm3F_switch:
Hittable switch block in the mine main chamber — a hit counter.

Displays as enemy sprite frame #0F with stat entry 118 and $FF HP. Each of the four placements zeroes the byte $0A01 when it spawns, so the counter starts at 0 in every visit. When attacked (hit callback) it shows the pressed sprite frame #11 and adds 1 to $0A01 (the scratch flags $08-$0F of scene $3F read as one byte); HP resets to $FF every frame so it can be hit repeatedly.

The counter is not tied to a particular switch or laborer: dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger fires when the byte equals 4.
dm40_hidden_dark_space:
Hidden Dark Space portal in the collapsed tunnel (map $40).

Checks event flag $0132 — if not set, waits and rechecks each frame.
Once the flag is set (tunnel cleared), spawns a Dark Space portal
with config $2B00 (type=1, displayMode=$2000) and despawns self.
dm40_trapped_slave:
Trapped laborer in the collapsed tunnel — breaks free when attacked.

Displays as a solid enemy sprite (spriteset_pickups_effects frame #00) with
$FF HP and stat entry 118. Cannot actually be killed — HP resets
each frame. Scratch flag $00 is set while the player stands in tiles (08,14)-(0A,17) and cleared otherwise. A hit while playerFlags bit $0002 is set (RunAttackFlagSetup: Psycho Slider, Psycho Dash or run attack) frees him: debris burst, then the rescue below.
After rescue, flag $D9 is set and the actor redraws 6 background
metatiles to show the cleared rubble, then gives 3 Red Jewels
(BCD add to jewelsCollected) with thank-you dialog.
dm41_bat_spawner:
Bat spawner in the mine zigzag area — periodically spawns homing mines.

Invisible actor that loops: waits until offscreen is false (#0D),
plays a 3-frame opening animation (frames #2F → #30 → #31), spawns
a dm_follower_behavior child at relative offset (0, -$32) that
chases the player, then waits $3B frames before repeating.
dm41_solid_wall_setup:
Initial wall tile setup for the mine zigzag area (map $41).

Draws solid metatile #05 at two positions (column $26 row 1, and
column $22 row 1), then marks both tiles as solid-high collision.
Used to block off passages before the player clears them. Despawns
immediately after drawing.
dm44_cell_door:
Double-locked cell door in the mine foyer — requires both mine keys.

Displays as a door sprite with interaction. When examined, checks
inventory for items #0B (Mine Key) and #0C (second key). If neither
key is present, shows "There are two keyholes" text. If only one key,
shows "Without both keys" message. If both keys present, offers a
Yes/No choice to use them. On Yes, removes both keys from inventory,
sets flags $5B and $5C, applies BG change #7A to open the door.
dm45_key:
Mine Key pickup in the morgue room (map $45).

Displays as a key sprite (spriteset_pickups_effects frame #02) that bobs
in a slow idle loop ($EF frame wait). Interactable — gives item
#0B (Mine Key) with SFX and "You found the Mine Key!" fanfare.
If inventory is full, shows the full-inventory message instead.
Sets flag $5D after pickup; despawns if flag already set.
dm47_imas:
Imas — chained slave in the mine inner room (map $47).

Spawns as a chain prop (dm_mine_static_prop) with solid collision and dies at spawn when flag $5E is set (tested once, not waited on). Before the chain breaks (status bit $0040 of the prop) the interact handler says "Cut the chain!". After it breaks he says that his homeland has people turned to stone and sick with unknown diseases. One of three chained slaves with Remus and Sam; Sam's talk handler sets $5E when he gives the Memory Melody, not the freeing of the third slave.
dm47_remus:
Remus — chained slave in the mine inner room (map $47).

Same structure as Imas: chain prop, "Cut the chain!" before the chain breaks, a thank-you dialog after. He asks Will to visit his home village across the ocean and help the villagers regain their strength. Dies at spawn when flag $5E is set (tested once, not waited on); Sam's talk handler sets $5E.
dm47_sam:
Sam — chained slave who teaches the Memory Melody after he is freed.

Spawns as a chain prop (dm_mine_static_prop) with solid collision and dies at spawn when flag $5E is set. Before the chain breaks (status bit $0040 of the prop) the interact handler says "Cut the chain!". After it breaks the handler tells Will about a song that restores lost memories. When $5E is still clear it then gives item #0D (Memory Melody) and sets $5E; with a full inventory it prints the inventory-full message and leaves $5E clear. A repeat talk after $5E is set says "I'll never forget you!".

Sam's main script waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #5E, #01 ), locks the joypad, starts music #1E, waits #77 ticks and polls APUIO1 for $FF (the track has finished). If Will holds the Wind Melody (#08), Sam asks for it and the Prison Key as souvenirs and removes #02 and #08; otherwise he asks for the Prison Key and removes #02. The joypad is then unlocked. Imas and Remus read $5E only once, at spawn.
fr32_alley_guard:
Guard blocking the Freejia back alley (scene $32).

Solid actor with a talk handler. The handler compares playerXPos ($09A2) with the guard's own X position ($14): below it prints 'Children don't come here. Go home.'; at or above it prints 'This kid! Where did you come from?! Go home! Go home!!' and sets scratch flag $01, on which the guard's main script clears its solid mark, writes $FFFB to playerSpeedEw ($09B2), waits #1D, clears the flag and marks itself solid again. No story flag is tested.
fr32_bg_sprite_a:
Background decorative sprite A in Freejia town.

Non-interactive animated sprite for street ambiance. No dialog.
fr32_bg_sprite_b:
Background decorative sprite B in Freejia town.

Non-interactive animated sprite for street ambiance. No dialog.
fr32_bg_sprite_c:
Background decorative sprite C in Freejia town.

Non-interactive animated sprite with different frame count.
No dialog.
fr32_creep:
Creepy man in Freejia — sinister dialog about understanding the city.

NPC with flag-gated states. Initial dialog: "Ha ha ha. You
understand this place. Sometimes what you think is unimportant."
Later: shorter "Ha ha ha." Hints at the dark underbelly of
Freejia's slave trade.
fr32_doomsday:
Doomsday prophet in Freejia — warns about the comet.

NPC who says: "Soon a great power will come from above...
Then mankind will die out." Foreshadows the comet threat
that drives the main plot.
fr32_fragrance:
Woman commenting on Freejia's city flower.

Simple NPC. Says: "The Freejia is the city flower. Smells
good, doesn't it?" Lighthearted contrast to the slave trade
happening behind the scenes.
fr32_guide:
Hotel guide man in Freejia (scene $32) — leads Will and Kara to the hotel.

Flag $57 clear: spawns the door actor code_05B315 (it opens on scratch flag $05). With $64 clear the guide waits for scratch $02 (set by fr32_kara), walks (StageSpriteLoopMove), prints 'What a cute couple... Have you decided where you're staying tonight?', clears $02, waits for scratch $03, walks to the hotel door and falls into code_05B1F1, where it stands at tile (28,25) with the talk line 'Well, come in.'; with $64 set it starts at code_05B1F1. Flag $57 set: stands at tile (29,24) with the 'Business is terrible' line and spawns town_door.TownDoorInit. The guide sets no flag.
fr32_herb:
Herb pickup item in Freejia town.

Collectible item actor. When interacted: "You found the herbs!"
If inventory is full: shows the full-inventory message.
Standard item pickup pattern with flag tracking.
fr32_honest_life:
Philosopher NPC in Freejia — reflects on honest living.

Simple NPC. Says: "A life lived honestly. A life of fun and
laughter." Provides moral contrast to the corruption theme.
fr32_hotel_hint:
Woman near the hotel — hints about the kidnapped worker.

NPC who says: "A man working at the hotel was caught by
a labor trader." Hints at the slave trade infiltrating
everyday life in Freejia.
fr32_hp_jewel:
HP Jewel pickup in Freejia town.

Stat-boosting collectible. Displays: "You found the HP jewel!"
Grants a permanent HP increase. Standard jewel pickup pattern.
fr32_idle_npc_a:
Idle animated NPC A in Freejia — ambient town resident.

Non-interactable NPC with looping idle animation for
town atmosphere. No dialog.
fr32_idle_npc_b:
Idle animated NPC B in Freejia — ambient town resident.

Non-interactable NPC with looping idle animation. No dialog.
fr32_kara:
Kara in Freejia town — excited about the city, story progression.

Multi-state NPC with extensive dialog branching. Initial state:
"Oh, it's nice!! What a great city!!!" — enthusiastic about
Freejia. Later: "Don't you like it, Will!! Let's go!!"
Manages flag-based story progression as the party explores
the city together.
fr32_kidnapper:
Door of the back-street house where Erik is held (scene $32, from Sam's dialog) and the voice behind it.

First-phase actor (code_05B371): flag $67 set -> dies. Otherwise marks tile (04,0D) solid, waits while off-screen and, when Will enters tiles (05,0E)-(0B,12), moves its sprite, spawns the door actor code_05B3A1 at pixel (0048,00E0) and dies. The door actor is a solid door sprite (spriteset_npc_props frame #01) with a talk handler: flag $66 (Sam told Will) clear prints 'Man's voice: If you don't want to lose your lives, go home!!'; $66 set prints the same line plus Will asking about Erik, sets $67 and marks tiles (08,0E)-(08,11) solid. Once $67 is set the door actor copies palette data, sets joypad mask bit $2000, clears playerFlags bit $0008, calls EnemyInitBasic with HP 5, sets bit $0100 and clears bit $1000 of $10, and prints 'If I don't save Erik...' while Will stands on tiles (07,0E)-(08,12). What a hit does afterwards is the common enemy code, not read here.
fr32_laborer_npc:
Walking laborer NPC in Freejia — animated background character.

Non-interactable NPC that walks a patrol route through town.
No dialog. Represents the laborers visible in Freejia's streets.
fr32_locked_door:
Locked door in Freejia (scene $32).

Solid door actor. It tests no flag and applies no background change. At spawn, when Will is within #01 tile (BranchIfPlayerNear), it shows frame #00, sets the joypad lock ($CFFC) for #1D ticks and plays sound #0E; then (and otherwise at once) it shows frame #01, marks itself solid and sets the talk handler, which always prints 'It's locked from the inside...'.
fr32_showman:
Street performer/showman in Freejia — entertainment NPC.

NPC who boasts: "No one can put on a show like I can.
Have a look!" Interactable with an animation sequence showing
his performance. Town color/atmosphere character.
fr32_slap:
Slap scene — NPC reacts to someone falling from the ceiling.

Event NPC: "I was startled... Someone dropped from the ceiling."
After: "Slap!!!!!! Kids! If you do something this dangerous
again..." — an adult NPC catches and scolds Will for a
dangerous stunt. Physical comedy scene.
fr32_slaver1:
Slave trader 1 in Freejia — searching for escaped laborer.

Patrolling NPC who says: "Where'd he go..." Part of the
labor escape subplot. Walks a route searching for the
laborer who escaped.
fr32_slaver2:
Slave trader 2 in Freejia — interrogates Will about the escapee.

Interactive NPC (~97 lines). Asks: "A laborer escaped. Have you
seen him? Yes/No" — dialog branches based on player choice.
If Yes, says "Where?!"; if No: "Hmm. Tell me if you see him."
Multi-state with flag progression tracking the escaped
laborer subplot.
fr32_walking_npc:
Walking town resident in Freejia — ambient patrol NPC.

Non-interactable NPC with a walk animation loop. No dialog.
Provides street life ambiance.
fr33_erik:
Erik imprisoned in Freejia — rescue cutscene.

Erik is held captive. On first interaction: "Impossible! You've
come to rescue me!!" Triggers the rescue sequence with flag
checks and joypad lock. Key story event where the party
reunites with Erik after his capture.
fr35_slave1:
Chained slave in the Freejia labor cells — resigned dialog.

Static NPC. Says: "Soon we will be sent away..." Represents
one of the laborers awaiting sale in the slave market.
fr35_slave2:
Chained slave in the Freejia labor cells — broken spirit dialog.

Static NPC. Says: "I've tried not to think. The more I think,
the more empty I become..." One of the emotionally heavy NPCs
in the slavery theme.
fr35_slave3:
Chained slave in the Freejia labor cells — lost faith dialog.

Static NPC. Says: "I don't believe in the spirits. If there
were spirits, things like this wouldn't happen." Challenges
the game's spiritual themes through hopelessness.
fr36_mother:
Worried mother NPC in Freejia.

Says: "Mothers are always worrying about things. I was afraid
you'd been kidnapped." Reflects the town's awareness of the
labor trade threat to children.
fr37_caution:
Cautious townsperson near Thorn Tower — warns about back streets.

NPC who warns: "Listen to me carefully. You'd better not go
on the back streets." Foreshadows the danger of the slave
trade area behind Freejia's pleasant facade.
fr38_ashamed:
Woman in the Adequacy Manor — apologizes for the mess.

Simple NPC. Says: "The upstairs is a mess... I'm ashamed..."
One of the manor residents.
fr38_boyfriend:
Boyfriend NPC in the Adequacy Manor — caught in a comic scene.

NPC with a single talk line (no flag test). Says: "She, uh, was just helping
me... Ha ha ha." Part of the couple joke sequence with the
girlfriend NPC.
fr38_girlfriend:
Girlfriend NPC in the Adequacy Manor — matching comic scene.

Counterpart to the boyfriend NPC. Says: "He had something in
his eye... Ha ha ha." Both give excuses when found together.
fr39_erik:
Erik at the Freejia hotel — reunited, suggests visiting the inventor.

After rescue: "It is good to be among friends again." Later:
"Well, there's an eccentric inventor in the woods nearby.
Shall we visit?" — hints at Neil's cottage and the Nazca
area. Flag-gated dialog progression.
fr39_kara:
Kara at the Freejia hotel — reunites with Lilly, reflects on events.

Multi-dialog NPC. Initial: "Lilly? Is it Lilly?!" — emotional
reunion with the spirit companion. Later: "I am glad everyone
is safe, but..." — hints at lingering concerns about the
slave trade.
fr39_lance:
Lance at the Freejia hotel — amnesia subplot after Incan ship escape.

Complex NPC (~117 lines). Says: "They say I don't know who I am.
Kind of strange..." Later: "What is this place?" — Lance has
amnesia from hitting his head. Kara comments: "Somehow I feel
a little..." Dialog tracks the Memory Melody quest to cure him.
fr39_lily:
Lilly at the Freejia hotel — manages the party reunion scene.

Multi-state NPC (~95 lines). Initial: "Come in... Will and Kara?!"
Later explains: "Lance hit his head escaping from the Incan
ship... The doctor says..." — establishes Lance's amnesia
and the need for the Memory Melody.
fr3A_harborer:
Man harboring the escaped laborer — afraid of being discovered.

NPC in the harborer's house. Says: "There was nothing he could
do about being found. He's the laborer who ran away..." Links
to the escaped laborer subplot from the slave traders.
fr3A_sympathetic:
Sympathetic woman harboring the laborer — begs for secrecy.

NPC pleading: "Please! Don't tell! I don't care about myself,
I just don't want to get this man in trouble." Emotional
scene showing civilians resisting the slave trade.
fr3B_tornado:
Messy house resident — humorous dialog about the mess.

NPC in a cluttered house. Says: "It's not like a tornado came
through here. Maybe you'd be more comfortable elsewhere."
Light humor scene.
fr3C_imas:
Imas in the Freejia slave market — enslaved villager from Asia.

Says: "I am Imas. I was brought here by boat from far-off Asia.
We are a hunting people..." Provides backstory about the
international scope of the labor trade. One of three named
slaves (with Remus and Sam) from the Diamond Mine.
fr3C_man1:
Bystander 1 in the slave market — uncomfortable observer.

NPC who says: "When I think of myself in your position, I
shudder. I've no time to worry about others." Shows the
moral compromises of Freejia's citizens.
fr3C_man2:
Bystander 2 in the slave market — admonishes Will to remember.

NPC: "These laborers are the same age as you. Remember.
There are people everywhere in worse situations." One of
the game's moral messaging NPCs.
fr3C_remus:
Remus in the Freejia slave market — tells about famine and hunting.

Multi-state NPC. Says: "I am Remus. Our game disappeared and
we had nothing to eat. We had no choice." Later: "How can
things like this happen?" Provides context about why people
were vulnerable to the slavers.
fr3C_sam:
Sam in the Freejia slave market — mentions Erik's rescue attempt.

NPC who says: "I am Sam. We were rescued last night by a man
named Erik who was working here..." Links the slave market
to Erik's capture subplot. Key information NPC.
fr3C_slaver:
Slave market guard (scene $3C).

Solid guard with a talk handler: prints 'Hey, boy! Kids can't come here! Go home! Go home! Or did you come to get a laborer?' with a Yes/No choice. No (or cancel) prints 'Go home! Go home!'. Yes prints 'I like your courage! I don't know what you'd do here, but have a look around.' and sets scratch flag $01; the main script then clears its solid mark, steps aside (StageSpriteMoveX) and shows frame #1A. No story flag is tested.
gs2A_shira:
Will's mother Shira in the dream sequence on the Gold Ship.

Emotional dream cutscene where Will sees his mother. Spawns a
background star effect actor, configures window masking (W12SEL,
WOBJSEL) for the dream visual effect, and plays the mother's
dialog about the comet: "Look in the sky. The comet is so
beautiful." Key early story moment establishing the comet theme.
gs2B_bones:
Skeleton on the wrecked ship — with dialog about the shipwreck.

Solid NPC using spriteset_npc_props frame #02 (bone sprite).
Positioned at (0, +4). When examined, provides flavor text
about the wrecked ship's history.
gs2B_erik:
Erik on the wrecked Gold Ship — scared reaction and dungeon event.

Before flag $51: solid NPC with interaction dialog about being
surprised. After flag $51: involved in a longer sequence using
camera_drift for screen shake and cameraTargetY adjustments.
Uses chatPtr, orbitAngle, orbitDiameter for state tracking.
Dialog: "I was surprised!! Oh, it's you, Will."
gs2B_seth:
Seth on the wrecked Gold Ship — gives a Red Jewel.

Before flag $51: solid NPC with interaction. On first talk
(flag $E0 not set): Seth found a strange jewel on board and
gives it to Will (hidden_red_jewel). After giving the jewel,
dialog changes to: "It's the first time I've ever given you
anything. Take care of it." Despawns after flag $51.
gs2B_wreck_wave_motion:
Wave motion parallax controller for the Gold Ship scenes.

Placed in scenes $2B-$2F (the wreck, the ship deck, the wreck interior, the gold interior and the adrift scene). At spawn it subtracts $20 from cameraDeltaY in scenes $2D and $2E only (the test is scene >= $2D and < $2F). Each frame it adds orbitAngle to cameraDeltaY while orbitDiameter counts down, to create the visual effect of the ship bobbing on waves; in scene $2F it then copies cameraDeltaY to cameraTargetY. Uses chatPtr, orbitAngle and orbitDiameter for sinusoidal wave timing.
gs2C_crew1:
Gold Ship deck crew member 1 — greets the "King" on arrival.

Simple solid NPC with interaction: "King! You're safe! Now we
can set sail." The crew believes Will is their lost king.
gs2C_crew2:
Gold Ship deck crew member 2 — animated patrol NPC.

Crew member who paces back and forth on deck with a multi-step
walk animation (frames #05-#09, alternating Y and X movement).
Pauses at solid positions with idle loop, then resumes patrol.
Interactable with celebratory dialog about the happy occasion.
gs2C_crew3:
Gold Ship deck crew member 3 — another pacing NPC.

Similar patrol animation to crew2 but uses different sprite
frames (#0C-#11). Walks a route and pauses at solid positions.
Provides crew dialog.
gs2C_crew4:
Gold Ship deck crew member 4 — static NPC with King reaction.

Solid NPC. Dialog: "It's the King! You're safe!" followed by
Will's inner thought: "(I'm the King???)" — showing Will's
confusion about being mistaken for royalty.
gs2C_crew5:
Gold Ship deck crew member 5 — variant NPC with conditional placement.

Checks flags $4E and $F8 for placement — if both set, shifts
position +$20 X. Reuses gs2C_crew4 dialog setup. Says: "Look,
look! The King has returned! And he's much shorter!"
gs2C_crow_crew:
Crow's nest lookout of the Gold Ship. The phases are keyed on two event flags: $4C (set by gs2C_descent when the ship leaves the cave) and $4F (set by this actor's first interaction).

Flag $4F already set at spawn: no sequence runs; the actor clears bit $2000 of its flag word, sets musicRoomGroup to 2 and idles (SetEntryHere + RTL).

Flag $4F clear: the actor waits for flag $4C, spawns the child code_05857A and clears bit $2000 of its flag word. The child writes TM $15, CGADSUB $A1 and COLDATA $E0 every frame (dark cave tint) until flag $4F is set, then dies. The interaction handler code_0584A9 prints the guard's "the ship is coming out of the cave" line on the first talk and sets flag $4F; later talks print the closing line.

Flag $4F set while waiting: the lookout masks the joypad (joypadMaskStd), starts music $03, waits 2 ticks and a vblank, clears backdropColors, writes COLDATA $FF, TM $17 and CGADSUB $A2, waits 60 ticks, spawns oneshot_backdrop_fade_out_1C (the backdrop ramp), waits 192 ticks, writes CGADSUB $22, waits 120 ticks, prints the closing line and releases the joypad mask. vblank_joypad supplies the vblank wait.
gs2C_descent:
Ship departure sequence — the Gold Ship leaves the cave (scene $2C).

Flag $4C clear: sets the joypad lock ($EFFC), sets the word flag $0185, writes TM = $15, CGADSUB = $B1 and COLDATA = $FF, places Will at pixel (D0,20) and starts player_character.loc_02C63B on him, then tests each frame (SetEntryHere) whether Will is at (D0,240). There it sets the joypad lock again, spawns oneshot_backdrop_fade_out_1C, waits #BF, sets $4C, prints 'This is the Incan Gold Ship?!', releases the joypad lock and dies.

Flag $4C set: the actor dies at once (code_0581FD). No music command is run by this actor.
gs2C_rain_particle:
Individual rain drop particle during the storm sequence.

Tiny actor that spawns at (-8, 0) offset from the spawner
and falls. Idle loop — no movement logic of its own;
position is set by the spawner.
gs2C_rain_spawner:
Rain spawner for the Gold Ship storm — spawns rain drop particles.

Loops every $0F frames, spawning a rain_particle child actor
with flags $0B00. Each spawned particle gets a random X offset
from the player position (RngByte - $80 + playerXPos) using
spriteset_pickups_effects and sprite priority #30.
gs2D_kara:
Kara in the wrecked Gold Ship interior (scene $2D).

Solid NPC with two talk handlers, switched by scratch flag $02 (set by gs2D_mummy's dialog): before it she says 'They perished waiting for the King's return...'; after it she says only 'What . . . ?'.
gs2D_lance:
Lance in the wrecked Gold Ship interior (scene $2D) — triggers the Seth cutscene on approach.

Before scratch flag $01 (set by gs2D_mummy's first talk): solid NPC at its spawn tile with the talk handler code_059028. After flag $01: clears the solid mark, moves to tile (0F,0D) (frame #05) and tests each frame whether Will is within 3 tiles (BranchIfPlayerNear). When Will is near it sets the joypad lock ($EFFC), prints 'Are you OK?', waits #3B, shakes the camera with camera_drift (CameraDriftLoopShip), waits #B3, prints Seth's scream with Lance's reply, sets persistent flag $51, removes the talk handler, walks off, releases the joypad lock and dies.
gs2D_lily:

hdma_circle_window_thinker:
Circular HDMA window generator (spotlight / iris) and its two thinkers (391960-392913, Bank 05).

It builds a per-scanline table of left and right edges for PPU window 1: QueueHdma uses hdma_channel_config entry #26 (WH0, $2126; transfer mode 1 = two registers, so every scanline writes WH0 = left edge and WH1 = right edge). The edges describe a filled circle, so the window is a circle that can move and grow or shrink. Lines outside the circle get the "empty window" value (left $FF, right $00: left > right, nothing is inside). Nothing here touches brightness or colour.

=== PARAMETERS (direct page $F4-$FE, written by the scene scripts) ===

  $F6 = circle centre X in screen pixels       ($F4 = the value used for the last build)
  $FA = circle centre Y in scanlines            ($F8 = the value used for the last build)
  $FE = radius in pixels                        ($FC = the value used for the last build)

A negative radius switches the circle off: the builder leaves the default table (one line of empty window, then end of table). The "previous" copies are refreshed by HdmaParamChangeCheck. While HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2 runs, $FC is reused as the circle decision variable; the V2 thinker restores it afterwards with HdmaCopyCurrentToPrev.

Writers: sF7_credits sets centre ($80, $7F) with radius $FFFF (off) and later raises the radius from 0 to $3F; gs2A_shira sets centre ($40, $40) and radius $120 (the circle is larger than the screen), then dream_zoom_controller moves the centre to the screen position of world point ($88, $180) (X from bg1ScrollH, Y from mapScrollV) and shrinks the radius by 2 per frame from $A0 until it falls below $40 (measured in the dream scene: the centre is ($88, $160) on screen, below the last visible line, so the lit area is a cap at the bottom edge that has left the screen after about 18 frames; from then on every visible line has the empty window and BG1, BG2 and the sprites stay hidden while BG3, the HUD, stays); mu67_male_vampire sets radius $FFFF at its start and at its end, a 32-iteration loop in mu67_vampires (address 718387) raises it by 1 per frame while sub_0AF6D7 copies the vampire actor's screen position into the centre. sF7_credits and gs2A_shira also set W12SEL to $33 themselves: window 1 enabled and inverted on BG1 and BG2, so with the display preset's TMW = $17 both layers show only inside the circle and are hidden outside it. gs2A_shira also writes WOBJSEL = $03 (window 1 enabled and inverted for sprites), so there the sprites are hidden outside the circle as well; the credits leave WOBJSEL at 0, so sprites stay visible everywhere. The window setup of the Mu scene is in mu67_vampires (address 718141, mu_color_window_setup, spawned by mu67_male_vampire at its start, address 717306): it writes WOBJSEL = $30 (colour window 1, enabled and inverted), CGWSEL = $22 (colour math prevented inside the window area, which is the part outside the circle; the sub screen is the addend) and CGADSUB = $03 (add to BG1 and BG2); W12SEL stays 0. While the radius is $FFFF the table is empty, so the whole screen is inside the window area and no colour math runs; with a circle the colour math (the fixed colour added to BG1 and BG2) runs only inside it.

=== THINKERS (scene_thinkers) ===

circle_window_thinker_v1 (variant 1): spawned only by scene F7 (credits). Every frame it calls HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1, then queues whichever table the double buffer selects.
circle_window_thinker_v2 (variant 2): spawned by scenes 2A (Gold Ship dream) and 67 (Mu vampire lair). It clears the previous-parameter copies once (HdmaInitPrevState), so the first frame builds only if one of the current centre X, centre Y or radius ($F6, $FA, $FE) is non-zero; then each frame compares current and previous parameters, rebuilds with HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2 only when something changed, copies current to previous and queues the table.

=== DOUBLE BUFFER AND MEMORY LAYOUT ===

HdmaParamChangeCheck adds 1 to chatPtr ($7F000A,X) on every change; bit 0 chooses the buffer the builder writes and the thinker queues (odd = buffer A, even = buffer B), so a table that HDMA is still reading is never rebuilt in place.
  buffer A: HDMA table at $7E7000, row data centred on $7E7600 (the builder's $00 pointer)
  buffer B: HDMA table at $7E7100, row data centred on $7E7A00
  $7E7200: the shared "empty window" word ($00FF); the builder keeps its address in $04
The table is an indirect HDMA table of 3-byte entries (line count, data pointer). Entries with a count below $80 hold one data word for that many lines (used for the empty lines above the circle: HdmaEmitHoldSegments); entries with bit 7 set are repeat mode, so HDMA fetches a new data word on every scanline (the circle rows: HdmaEmitRepeatSegments). Both splitters cap a segment at 127 lines.

=== CIRCLE ALGORITHM (HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2) ===

A Bresenham-style integer circle. x starts at the radius (rounded down to even), y at 0 and the decision variable $FC at the radius. For each y it stores the word (left = centreX - x, right = centreX + x, each clamped to 0..255) on the rows centre + y and centre - y of the data area, then the transposed pair (row x with half-width y); then $FC = $FC - (2y - 1) and, when $FC goes negative, $FC = $FC + 2(x - 1) and x = x - 1. It stops when x < 0 or x < y. Rows beyond +-255 are skipped (the data area holds 256 words per side), so a radius over $FF is only drawn for its central rows. Rows near the top and bottom of the circle come out a few pixels wider than an ideal circle.
The table is laid out as: lines above the circle (hold entries), the circle rows (repeat entries, 2 data bytes per line), then a final one-line empty entry and the end marker. When the circle is cut off by the top of the screen the first visible row starts at the matching data row; a circle entirely above the screen emits only the final empty entry.

HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1 follows the same structure but with different row arithmetic (see its part note): it spans only radius + 1 lines vertically and stores the row words at a one-byte stride. Measured on the credits screen: the radius grows by 1 per frame from 0 to $3F and then stays there; the lit area is a filled oval centred on ($80, $7F), about 125 pixels wide (x = $42-$BE at radius $3F) and 63 scanlines tall (96-158), with the picture inside and black outside. It is not a set of thin slivers.

=== HELPERS ===
  HdmaEmitHoldSegments - emit hold entries (count 1-127, data pointer $04 = the empty word) for a number of lines
  HdmaEmitRepeatSegments - emit repeat-mode entries (count | $80) whose data pointer advances through the row data by 2 bytes per line
  HdmaParamChangeCheck - compare current and previous parameters; on change store them, toggle the buffer, set the write pointers and the empty word
  HdmaNoChange - return carry set
  HdmaInitPrevState - zero the previous centre X, centre Y and radius
  HdmaCompareParams - carry clear = something changed
  HdmaCopyCurrentToPrev - previous = current
na49_camera:
Camera object in Neil's cottage — invention description.

Interactive object: "That's a camera. It will burn a copy of a
scene onto printing paper. The problem is that it takes too
long." Shows Neil's invention progress. Early photography
concept in the game's pseudo-historical setting.
na49_erik:
Erik at Neil's cottage — mentions Seth.

NPC: "Seth will be pleased when he sees this invention..."
Erik's reaction to Neil's camera invention. References
Seth from the Gold Ship chapter.
na49_kara:
Kara at Neil's cottage — conflicts with Neil.

Extended NPC (~60 lines). "I can't believe it! I don't want to
breathe the same air as him!" Later: "Cygnus?! Neil: That's
the Tower of Babel..." Kara's personality clashes with Neil's
analytical nature. Also references the Tower of Babel.
na49_lance:
Lance at Neil's cottage — short hair joke.

Extended NPC (~73 lines). "I've only had mine on for three
weeks. I guess I lose!" Later: "We're going, too! We don't
want Will to be the only one having a good time."
The group decides to join the expedition.
na49_lily:
Lilly at Neil's cottage — Kara insults Neil's smell.

Extended NPC (~84 lines). Kara: "This person stinks..."
Lilly: "What are you saying! You shouldn't talk like that!!
There's a wonderful smell in this house." Lilly defends
Neil against Kara's rudeness. Character dynamics.
na49_neil:
Neil at his cottage — reunion and expedition planning.

Major NPC (~135 lines). "It's open, come in. Will: Neil.
It's me. Will from South Cape." Neil: "Oh! Will! You've
gotten strong! Are all of these people your friends?"
The reunion at Neil's cottage. Leads to planning the
Nazca expedition and eventually the Sky Garden trip.
na49_tank:
Oxygen tank in Neil's cottage — invention display.

Interactive object. Neil: "That's an oxygen tank. There's air
inside. With this you can breathe underwater, but it only
works for a short time." Foreshadows the undersea tunnel
and Mu underwater exploration.
na49_telescope:
Telescope in Neil's cottage — stargazing invention.

Interactive object: "That's a telescope. You can see stars
as if they were in your hand." Shows Neil's scientific
instruments. Connects to the comet observation theme.
na49_wings:
Airplane wings in Neil's cottage — the flying machine.

Interactive object. Neil: "Those are airplane wings. It's part
of a machine that will fulfill man's dream of flying."
Foreshadows Neil's airplane used in the Sky Garden descent
and the Tower of Babel approach.
na4B_buried_tile:
Buried tile discovery at Nazca — the ground painting puzzle.

Key story event (~128 lines). "There's a tile buried in the
sand... When Will's Flute touched it, there was a rumbling
sound." Neil: "Will! Don't look yet! You don't know what's
in there!!" The Flute reveals a buried tile that is part
of the Nazca ground painting discovery. Triggers the
Sky Garden revelation sequence.
na4B_erik:
Erik at Nazca — scared but curious.

Multi-state NPC. Initially: "It's scary... I'll stay with
Neil." Later: "What's going to happen? It's exciting!"
Erik's evolving reaction from fear to excitement about
the Nazca discoveries.
na4B_kara:
Kara at Nazca — appreciates the artistry.

Extended NPC (~105 lines). "It must be great to paint such a
huge painting on a natural canvas." Later: "When you look at
it this way, it's like the white lines at an athletic event.
Maybe they're running lanes?" Kara's artistic perspective
on the Nazca lines.
na4B_lance:
Lance at Nazca — reflects on life's purpose.

NPC: "Up until now all I've done is go to school, study, and
play. Sometimes I wonder if my life has meaning." Lance's
philosophical moment. Later: "We're working on a puzzle that
explorers and archeologists have never solved..." Character
growth through the adventure.
na4B_lily:
Lilly at Nazca — wonders about the ancient builders.

Extended NPC (~110 lines). "The ancients were amazing. I wonder
why they made this..." Later: "Doesn't there seem to be a
pattern in the way the rocks are scattered around?" Lilly
provides the clue for the puzzle solution.
na4B_neil:
Neil at Nazca — the scientist's excitement.

Extended NPC (~114 lines). "It was a long way, but you did a
good job. This is the most famous of the ground paintings."
Later: "Ha ha ha. Don't be in such a hurry. Wait for everyone
else." Neil's scientific enthusiasm about the Nazca lines.
na4B_spirit:
Moon Tribe spirit at Nazca — ominous appearance.

NPC: "Ku ku ku..." The Moon Tribe's characteristic laugh.
Brief mysterious appearance hinting at the alien connection
to the Nazca lines and Sky Garden.
sg___hint_spirit:
Moon Tribe hint spirit in Sky Garden — combat advice.

Simple NPC that appears and gives the hint: "Attack when the
Crystal Bird cries." Provides the key strategy for the
Viper boss fight.
sg4C_platforms:
Floating platform controller for the Sky Garden main area.

Manages the moving platforms that the player rides between
garden sections (~116 lines). Handles platform spawn,
movement paths, player attachment/detachment, and the
rhythmic movement cycle of each platform.
sg4C_spirits:
Moon Tribe spirits in the Sky Garden main area — exposition NPCs.

Moon Tribe aliens who provide story context: "We meet again.
Ku ku ku. You're a strong boy to have come this far." and
"This Sky Garden is our mode of transportation. There are
four Crystal Birds..." Explain the Crystal Bird boss mechanic
and the Sky Garden's purpose.
sg4D_jump_handler:
Platform jump handler for Sky Garden floating platforms.

Manages the gap-jumping mechanic unique to Sky Garden. When
the player reaches a platform edge, handles the jump arc,
landing detection, and fall-off logic for the floating
garden platforms.
sg51_statue:
Movable statue in the garden southwest area (scene $51).

Movable statue: push_handler_solid pulls it one tile (16 px) toward the player while the player holds L or R (the shoulder pair $0030) on the same row, at least 32 px away and facing it. Observed as Will with no ability item or form needed (from the west and the east side; pulling along the column did not move either statue in the tests). Two placements, at tiles (30,33) and (30,34). Solid; HP resets to $FF every frame. A hit while playerFlags bit $0002 is set (RunAttackFlagSetup: Psycho Slider, Psycho Dash or run attack) jumps to StandardEnemyDefeatHandler and destroys it; any other hit leaves it standing. It reads and writes no event flag and tests no slot position.
sg52_blocker_enemy_a:
Toggle block A on the garden southwest underside (scene $52) — a hit switch, not an enemy to kill.

Two placements. Solid enemy sprite with stat entry 118; HP resets to $FF every frame, so it never dies. Each hit swaps between two states: frame #0F with BG change #90 and $0125/$0126 cleared, and frame #10 with BG change #26 and $0125/$0126 set. Both placements test $0126 every frame, so the one that was not hit follows the other and the two always show the same state. The state at spawn follows $0126.
sg52_blocker_enemy_b:
Toggle block B on the garden southwest underside (scene $52) — a hit switch, not an enemy to kill.

One placement. Solid enemy sprite with stat entry 118; HP resets to $FF every frame, so it never dies. Each hit swaps between frame #0F (BG change #28, sets $0127/$0128, clears $0129/$012A) and frame #10 (BG change #2A, sets $0129/$012A, clears $0127/$0128). At spawn it starts in frame #0F when $0127 is set and in frame #10 otherwise, without applying a BG change.
sg52_switch:
Knight-armor plate on the garden southwest underside (scene $52).

While flag word $012E is clear it tests each frame whether scene actor #3 (the pushable sg4F_knight_armor2, spawned at tile (38,33)) stands at pixel ($0258,$0330), the tile of the plate itself; when the player stands near it prints "When you step on this tile it makes a sound...". When the armor is there it applies BG change #2E and sets $012D and $012E. With $012E set (also at load) it places that actor exactly at ($0258,$0330), clears the solid mark at tile (38,32) and then idles.
sg54_pressure_switch:
Knight-armor plate on the garden west underside (scene $54).

Dies at spawn when flag word $012F is set. Otherwise it tests each frame whether scene actor #3 (the pushable sg4F_knight_armor4, spawned at tile (3A,2F)) stands at pixel ($0348,$02E0), the tile of the plate itself. When it does it applies BG change #2F, sets $012F and dies. The latch is permanent; nothing resets it when the armor is pushed away.
